thread:
morgan_sales: Quick heads up - Acme POC on Dedicated: SSO via Okta is failing for multiple users with 'Invalid audience' when they try to sign in. POC uses our dedicated pool (tenant acme-poc). Can someone triage?

devon_se: Can you paste the SP metadata / entityID and ACS you configured in Okta? audience mismatch is the usual culprit.

morgan_sales: Config we put in Okta: entityID = https://dedicated.acme.redwood.ai/saml/metadata
ACS URL = https://dedicated.acme.redwood.ai/saml/acs

li_engineer: Two quick checks: 1) Audience in the SAML assertion must exactly match the entityID (no trailing slash). 2) Signed cert in Okta matches the cert we expect.

morgan_sales: From our SAML logs: 'SAMLResponse validation failed: AudienceRestriction validation failed. expected https://dedicated.acme.redwood.ai/saml/metadata but got https://redwood-inference.com'

irene_cs: Customer says sometimes it looks like they get in then land on a 403 page. They tried refresh and same.

okta-bot: SCIM event: POST /Users -> 409 Conflict. payload: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"detail":"User already exists","status":"409"}

devon_se: 409 from SCIM usually means Okta is trying to create an account with an externalId we already have. If Okta is set to 'Create and update' it may be re-sending an existing user. Recommend toggling to 'Push only new users' while we debug.

morgan_sales: Also worth noting: customer tried using a Hosted API key (from the console) to test calls - just clarifying: POC Dedicated uses separate API keys and a different endpoint, so that won't help SSO.

li_engineer: Correct - hosted vs dedicated keys are different. For SAML fix, can you get a decoded SAMLResponse (base64) from the customer and paste the Audience element? If they don't want to paste whole assert, just the <Audience> text. Example:```xml
<saml:Conditions>
  <saml:AudienceRestriction>
    <saml:Audience>https://redwood-inference.com</saml:Audience>
  </saml:AudienceRestriction>
</saml:Conditions>
```

morgan_sales: I'll request the decoded assertion now. Also they mentioned group provisioning is flaky - Okta shows some SCIM requests returning 409 and some 201s.

irene_cs: Customer wants to know impact: will duplicate SCIM users break access to Dedicated pool?

devon_se: It can. If SCIM creates duplicate user objects with different externalIds or emails, the login routing can pick the wrong tenant mapping and then SAML assertion Audience won't match the tenant (leading to Invalid audience).

okta-bot: SCIM event: PATCH /Groups/acme-poc-users -> 200 OK (members updated)

li_engineer: Checklist for next steps (short):
- Confirm Okta Application 'Audience (Entity ID)' equals our tenant entityID exactly.
- Confirm ACS (Assertion Consumer Service) URL matches config.
- Ask customer to decode SAMLResponse and confirm <Audience> value.
- Check NameID format (we expect email).
- For SCIM: inspect 409 body for existing externalId and consider switching to update-only mode then reconcile users.

morgan_sales: I've asked Acme to: 1) decode SAMLResponse and send Audience, 2) share SCIM 409 response body, 3) try toggling provisioning create mode and re-sync.

devon_se: If they still fail, send me the raw base64 SAMLResponse and I'll decode and re-run our validation locally. Also drop the Okta app export settings (JSON) if possible.

morgan_sales: Customer also asked about VPC checklist for next phase - I told them we'll separate that convo (different thread) and flagged infra.

irene_cs: I'll track this on the customer side and confirm once they do the toggle. Thanks.

morgan_sales: Thanks team - will follow up once they send the assertion. :thumbsup:
